mcqs.question: Why does a typeahead system see roughly 20x more requests than the underlying search volume, for a 20-character average query?
options: Every user submits each search twice by default
getSuggestions fires on every keystroke while typing, not just once on submit, so request volume scales with characters typed
The typeahead service retries every request 20 times for reliability
Typeahead traffic is unrelated to search volume entirely
mcqs.explanation: Typeahead calls fire continuously as the user types, so a 20-character query generates roughly 20 suggestion requests versus one final search submission. There's no default double-submit and no 20x retry policy — this is just the natural fan-out of a per-keystroke feature, and it is directly tied to search volume, just multiplied.

mcqs.question: Why doesn't a typeahead system rebuild its entire trie every time a query starts trending?
options: Rebuilding the full trie is too slow/expensive to run continuously, so a lightweight fast-path counter service handles trending signals separately from the trie's slower rebuild cycle
Trending queries are ignored entirely in typeahead ranking
The trie is stored on disk specifically so it can be rebuilt instantly
Trending detection is handled by the client app, not the server
mcqs.explanation: A full trie rebuild is a heavy offline job; running it on every trending signal wouldn't scale. Instead, a fast, narrow path tracks trending counts separately and blends into serving, while the trie itself refreshes on its own slower cycle. Trending queries absolutely matter to ranking, the trie lives in memory (not disk, for latency), and this is a server-side design, not a client concern.

mcqs.question: Why is querying the live full-text search index directly, on every keystroke, a poor fit for typeahead at 2 million requests/sec?
options: Full-text search indexes cannot be queried by prefix at all
It would require rebuilding the index constantly
Search-and-rank cost per query is far higher than a precomputed trie traversal, and that cost multiplied by 2M req/sec is far more expensive than serving precomputed completions
Full-text indexes are only readable in batch, never in real time
mcqs.explanation: The core issue is cost per request multiplied by volume: live search-and-rank is inherently more expensive than an O(prefix length) trie lookup, and at 2M req/sec that difference dominates. Full-text indexes can support prefix-ish queries and can be read in real time — the problem is cost at this specific volume, not capability.
